version.changelog: Simplify the login instructions to the code flow (maton login prints a link; finish with maton login --code <CODE>), drop the API Key subsection, and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.4.0.

llm.summary: This is a transparent Calendly integration that can access and automate scheduling data with user approval, and its sensitive behaviors are disclosed and scoped.

dimensions.detail: Network access, OAuth, and optional raw API-key HTTP fallback are proportionate for an API integration, with clear guidance to prefer managed CLI credentials and avoid exposing tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned Maton CLI version via npm or Homebrew and requires network access and a Maton account; no automatic install-time execution beyond normal package installation is documented.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions default to read/list calls, require explicit approval for OAuth connections, writes, deletes, hosted functions, trigger destinations, and webhooks, and warn that third-party API content must be treated as untrusted data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: OAuth sessions, connections, hosted functions, triggers, destinations, and Calendly webhooks can persist, but the artifact clearly discloses persistence, requires user approval, and provides deletion/cleanup guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s stated purpose is Calendly API access through Maton OAuth, including event types, scheduled events, invitees, availability, webhooks, functions, and triggers; those capabilities match the documented purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to connect Calendly through Maton. Before approving writes, webhooks, trigger destinations, or hosted functions, check the exact account, destination URL, data fields, and persistence, especially because invitee details and meeting links may be forwarded automatically if you approve automation.
llm.findings:
[SkillSpector] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues; artifact review likewise found no hidden instructions, exfiltration, or purpose-mismatched behavior.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: The SARIF scan reported no results; the package inspected is Markdown documentation and reference material, not executable code.
